newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian 10-yr bond nudging on the rally.
newsitem.headline: Australian 10-yr bond nudging on the rally.

text.p: *Australian bonds stayed in a positive mood during a light morning session and will be looking to progress the rally further once key U.S. data is out of the way later on Friday.
*U.S. Treasuries brace for July payrolls report.

The Australian bond market remained in a positive mood during a relatively light morning session and will be looking to progress the rally once the key U.S. labour force report is out of the way later on Friday.

Ten-year bond futures edged to a new all-time high of 93.690, just surpassing the previous high of 93.680 seen in SYCOM, and taking the 10-year yield to its lowest level in nearly a quarter of a century.
"We saw some buying of long semi-stock which has given the market its lift in this latest move. It looks as if it wants to try out the 93.700s," one trader said.

Market friendly fundamentals and buoyant U.S. Treasuries continue to push yields lower, and although they are some 10 basis points lower on the week, any profits that needed to be taken where achieved after this week's official rate cut.
"(And) I suspect we are going to hold up at least until the Fannie Mae issue is priced," one trader added.

Fannie Mae issued its second global bond in Australian dollars on Thursday, and enthusiastic investor demand for the 10-year bond saw it increased from A$1.0 billion from an initial offering of A$750 million. The bonds will be priced in London later on Friday at 10 basis points over.

The local yield curve continued to flatten after this week's rate cut induced steepening with the long end gaining most from the strength of the U.S. market. New Zealand debt was again undermined by the plight of the N.Z. dollar.
